nodes.name: Ni foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: The Ni foam was firstly pre-cleaned by consecutively washing in 0.1 M of HCl aqueous solution, water, and ethanol under sonication followed by drying under the ambient condition.
nodes.source_text: The Ni foam was firstly pre-cleaned by consecutively washing in 0.1 M of HCl aqueous solution, water, and ethanol under sonication followed by drying under the ambient condition.

nodes.name: MH-TMO hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.5 mmol of Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, 0.5 mmol of Cu(NO3)2·6H2O, and 1.25 mmol of oxalic acid were added into 40 mL of H2O followed by sonication for 30 min to ensure the uniform dispersion. The obtained solution was then transferred into a Teflon reactor containing a piece of pre-cleaned Ni foam (2.5×3 cm). The reactor was kept at 200°C for 24 h. After the reaction, the Ni foam with in situ formed products was collected and washed by water and ethanol and then dried in vacuum at 60°C for 24 h.

nodes.name: Fe2O3 nanosheets hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: The pure Fe2O3 nanosheets on Ni foams were obtained in the same procedure as that of MH-TMO without adding Cu precursors. To keep the stoichiometric balance of metal and oxalate ions, the amounts of added oxalic acid were tuned to 1.5 mmol for the synthesis of Fe2O3 nanosheets on Ni foams.

nodes.procedure: The CuO polyhedrons on Ni foams were obtained in the same procedure as that of MH-TMO without adding Fe precursors. To keep the stoichiometric balance of metal and oxalate ions, the amounts of added oxalic acid were tuned to 1 mmol.
nodes.source_text: The pure Fe2O3 nanosheets and CuO polyhedrons on Ni foams were obtained in the same procedure as that of MH-TMO without adding Cu and Fe precursors, respectively. To keep the stoichiometric balance... 1 mmol.

nodes.name: MH-TMO
aliases: mesoporous and heterostructured transition metal oxides

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows vertical Fe2O3 nanosheets on Ni foam and sandwich structure of MH-TMO containing middle Fe2O3 nanosheets and CuO polyhedrons on both sides.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The synthesized Fe2O3 nanosheets with an average thickness of ≈30 nm are vertically grown on the nickel substrate (Figure 1b). The MH-TMO can be uniformly obtained with a sandwich structure containing middle Fe2O3 nanosheets and CuO polyhedrons on both sides (Figure 1f,g).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows mesoporous structure throughout Fe2O3 nanosheets and CuO polyhedrons in MH-TMO with average mesopore size of 4.6 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The mesoporous structure of Fe2O3 nanosheets was further characterized by TEM in Figure 1c,d. A large number of mesopores were observed... The mesopores with a large density can also be observed throughout the CuO (Figure 1h).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows Fe2O3 (110) lattice fringe with 0.24 nm spacing indicating <001> growth direction; MH-TMO interface shows Fe2O3 (110) and CuO (-111) both at 0.24 nm confirmed by FFT.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the high-resolution TEM image in Figure 1e, the lattice fringe with an interplanar spacing of 0.24 nm is assigned to the (110) plane... In the high-resolution TEM image in Figure 1i, the CuO displays the lattice fringe with an interplanar spacing of 0.24 nm corresponding to the CuO (-111) plane, while the Fe2O3 shows the lattice fringe with a similar value corresponding to the Fe2O3 (110) plane.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM EDS mapping confirms presence of Cu, Fe, O and separated signals of Fe and Cu elements in MH-TMO heterostructures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS mapping shows the presence of Cu, Fe and O, and the separated signals of Fe and Cu elements, supporting the successful formation of oxide heterostructures (Figure 1k).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms hematite phase for pure Fe2O3 nanosheets, tenorite phase for CuO polyhedrons, and both phases present in MH-TMO with overlapping peak at 35.7° for Fe2O3 (110) and CuO (-111).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The pure Fe2O3 nanosheets were identified to be a hematite phase, while the CuO polyhedrons have a tenorite phase. The MH-TMO has all the corresponding peaks of both phases.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Fe 2p3/2 shifts negatively in MH-TMO vs pure Fe2O3 at 712.3 eV; Cu 2p3/2 shows Cu2+ at 934.3 eV and Cu+ at 932.5 eV; O 1s shows increased oxygen vacancies in MH-TMO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the XPS spectrum of pure Fe2O3 nanosheets, Fe shows a fairly broad Fe 2p3/2 peak at around 712.3 eV... After the construction of MH-TMO, the binding energy of Fe 2p peaks negatively shifted. The Cu 2p3/2 peak at 934.3 eV is associated with the divalent Cu, while the peak at 932.5 eV indicates the presence of considerable Cu+.

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES confirms Fe oxidation state close to +3 in MH-TMO; EXAFS shows M–O and M–O–M bonds similar to Fe2O3 but with compressed M–O–M bond in MH-TMO due to Fe2O3-CuO interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe K edge spectra for MH-TMO with a relatively low pre-edge intensity supports that the oxidation state of Fe in MH-TMO is close to the value of +3... the MH-TMO shows no characteristic peaks of a metallic Fe–Fe bond, but has the M–O and M–O–M bonds similar to the Fe–O and Fe–O–Fe in Fe2O3.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows Fe–O vibrations at 220 and 403 cm⁻¹ in Fe2O3 and Cu–O at 289 and 650 cm⁻¹ in CuO within MH-TMO; post-OER shows weakened peaks and new MIII-OOH at 528 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectrum of MH-TMO indicates the vibration of Fe–O in Fe2O3 (220 and 403 cm⁻¹) and Cu-O in CuO (289 and 650 cm⁻¹). After OER measurement, those peaks weaken while the metal oxyhydroxide (MIII⋅OOH) formed with the new peak appearance at 528 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV determines double-layer capacitance Cdl for ECSA calculation; MH-TMO ECSA 2.1-2.7× larger than Fe2O3 and CuO despite ~20-50× higher OER activity indicating high intrinsic activity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) of the MH-TMO was then measured by the CV experiments at the non-Faradic range... The MH-TMO shows an electrochemically surface area only 2.1–2.7 times larger than the control samples... the specific current density (representing the intrinsic activity) of MH-TMO is 0.394 mA cm⁻², which is 19.7 and 26.3 times larger

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows MH-TMO has smallest charge transfer resistance ≈2 Ω indicating most efficient charge transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Nyquist plots were obtained in the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy analysis (EIS)... exhibiting that MH-TMO electrode has the smallest charge transfer resistance (≈2 Ω), indicating the most efficient charge transfer of MH-TMO.
